story_title: Antibiotic Resistance Patterns Among Pathogenic Bacteria
story_subtitle: Analyzing MIC values for Penicillin, Streptomycin, and Neomycin across Gram-stained bacteria genera

story_pieces.narration: Gram-negative bacteria exhibit significantly higher Penicillin MIC values compared to Gram-positive counterparts, with Aerobacter aerogenes (870 µg/mL) and Klebsiella pneumoniae (850 µg/mL) showing extreme resistance.
story_pieces.question: How do Penicillin MIC values differ between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (Gram stain vs. Penicillin MIC)

story_pieces.narration: Neomycin demonstrates variable efficacy across genera, with Streptococcus viridans (40 µg/mL) showing exceptionally high resistance while Brucella abortus (0.02 µg/mL) requires minimal concentrations.
story_pieces.question: Which bacterial genera exhibit the most extreme Neomycin MIC values?
story_pieces.visualization: scatter plot (genus vs. Neomycin MIC) with outlier highlighting

story_pieces.narration: Streptomycin resistance is more prevalent in Gram-negative species, with Escherichia coli (0.4 µg/mL) and Salmonella typhosa (0.4 µg/mL) requiring lower concentrations compared to Gram-positive Streptococcus viridans (40 µg/mL).
story_pieces.question: How does Streptomycin MIC vary between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria?
story_pieces.visualization: box plot (Gram stain vs. Streptomycin MIC)
